title: PtyRAD: A High-performance and Flexible Ptychographic Reconstruction Framework with Automatic Differentiation
content: Electron ptychography has advanced rapidly in recent years, consistently pushing the boundaries of resolution and enabling critical insights across diverse experimental conditions and material systems [1-4]. Although its theoretical foundation was established nearly 60 years ago [5] and refined through decades of incremental improvements, the technique only gained widespread adoption with the convergence of modern instrumentation, high-speed detectors [6-7], advanced algorithms [8-9], and increased computational power. Despite these advances, several challenges remain. First, many newly developed algorithms are implemented within individual research groups without public code or dataset sharing, hindering reproducibility and further innovation. Second, a significant portion of these developments relies on closed-source platforms like MATLAB, limiting accessibility and preventing the kind of broad, community-driven growth seen in open-source environments such as Python. Third, essential features and tools for electron ptychography are often fragmented across multiple software packages, making it difficult to integrate them seamlessly for comprehensive analysis and reconstruction.
